correctness.rationale: Fourier transform of e_x e_y=e_(2y−x) gives (vu)^∧(ψ)=v^(ψ^(−1))u^(ψ²). For idempotents cψ=cψ⁻¹ cψ², inversion-paired nonzero Fourier coefficients form 2x2 matrices [[0,cψ²],[cψ⁻²,0]] whose offdiagonal entries vanish together or are both nonzero; hence each is diagonalizable, including self-inverse scalar blocks. If no order-4 element exists, squaring on odd-character subgroup permutes finite cycles; idempotency forces products cηcη⁻¹∈{0,1} and all eigenvalues in {0,±1}. Explicit basis and uniform idempotents attain {0,±1} when odd order exists; exponent-2 core has trivial quandle and only eigenvalue1. Order-four character χ gives idempotent uλ=|G|⁻¹Σ(1+λχ²(g))e_g with spectrum containing ±λ for arbitrary complex λ. Independent exact arithmetic checked cyclic examples Z2,3,4,5,6,8 and complex λ values; this is finite corroboration, not an all-groups proof.
